messages:
julia: Hey - batch jobs hitting scheduling failures for gpu workloads in eu-west2. Pods show "0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" but several nodes report free GPUs in prometheus. Autoscaler didn't add nodes. Anyone seen this pattern?

omar: Can you paste `kubectl describe pod` for one failing pod and the CA events?

julia: Sure — here's the events from one pod:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/batch-job-42 to node-abc
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s   default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

I also ran `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME,GPUs,LABELED` (snippet):

```
node-1   4   nvidia.com/mig.enabled=true
node-2   4   nvidia.com/mig.enabled=true
node-3   4   nvidia.com/mig.enabled=false
node-4   4   nvidia.com/mig.enabled=false
node-5   4   nvidia.com/mig.enabled=false
node-6   0   <no-gpu>
```

sre-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp: failed to scale up: failed to launch instance for node-group batch-gpu-eu-west2: quotaExceeded: Insufficient instance quota for region eu-west2. Request: 4 GPUs (2 x n1-standard-16 with A100), Available: 0

deploy-bot: scale-up triggered for node-group batch-gpu-eu-west2 at 2026-03-18T12:45:20Z — failed (quota).

kevin: Two quick thoughts: 1) Mixed MIG and non-MIG pools can make the device plugin expose different resource names (e.g., `nvidia.com/gpu` vs `nvidia.com/gpu-mig.*`) so scheduler weight/advertising mismatch happens. 2) If pods were created for MIG units but landed on non-MIG nodes the plugin might not advertise the same resources -> Insufficient.

maria: We recently migrated node-1/2 to A100 and enabled MIG. Old pool (node-3/4/5) are RTX8000 (non-MIG). Our batch job specs request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and also set a `nodeAffinity` that unintentionally excludes some MIG nodes (legacy label mismatch).

omar: That explains it — autoscaler refused to scale target pool because CA target group only includes non-MIG nodegroup. CA logs show scale-up attempted against batch-gpu-eu-west2 (non-MIG) but our job needs MIG nodes.

kevin: Short fixes you can try right now:
- Add `nodeSelector: nvidia.com/mig.enabled: \"true\"` to the MIG-aware job to force scheduling onto MIG nodes.
- Or create a dedicated homogeneous node pool (A100 MIG) and point CA to it.
- If you need immediate capacity and CA is blocked by quota, consider running low-priority jobs on non-MIG nodes by removing strict affinity.

julia: We need something today — I'll patch the job to nodeSelector MIG=true and requeue. If CA still fails due to quota we'll need SRE to request a bump.

maria: Note: some pods in this workload use `nvidia.com/gpu-mig.count` via the device-plugin. Those will never run on the non-MIG pool. Also check for stray `nodeAffinity` on older job templates.

omar: Also check for `PodDisruptionBudget` or `topologySpreadConstraints` that might prevent packing. I saw a couple of jobs declare `maxSkew: 1` with strict topology that leaves GPUs fragmented across nodes.

kevin: For longer term:
- Use a MIG-only node pool and advertise per-MIG resources consistently.
- Consider packing small jobs into fewer nodes using the device-plugin's multi-container-per-GPU support when safe (MIG or mps).
- Add a scheduler-extender/profile that prefers binpacking by GPU memory/cores, not just free GPUs.
- CA config: ensure `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` and `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` are tuned and that CA is allowed to scale the MIG nodegroup.

sre-bot: Created ticket SRE-341 (quota bump request) and INC-1021 to track the MIG nodepool scheduling issue. Requested temporary on-demand quota for eu-west2.

maria: Also flagged a config drift: our node-labels used by helm charts were `gpu:mig=true` vs kernel's `nvidia.com/mig.enabled=true`. Fixing that will avoid accidental mismatch.

julia: Patch applied: added nodeSelector `nvidia.com/mig.enabled: \"true\"` and removed legacy nodeAffinity from batch-job template. Requeued 12 pods.

deploy-bot: 12 pods requeued. 2 pods immediately scheduled to node-1 and node-2, others pending.

omar: If pending persists after patch, do `kubectl describe node <candidate>` and `kubectl logs -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-<pod>` — plugin sometimes fails to advertise MIG slices after kernel update.

kevin: Long-term action items:
- Create a dedicated MIG node pool and point jobs there (product: MIG optimized).
- Update autoscaler profile to include the MIG node group and verify quotas.
- Add an alert for "scale-up failed due to quota" and for "insufficient nvidia.com/gpu with available GPU metrics" to catch mismatch earlier.

julia: Thanks — this should get the batches moving. I'll follow up on the ticket and keep you posted. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Acknowledged. Will follow up with quota owners and confirm CA now targets the correct node groups.
